content: Before taking levofloxacin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other quinolone antibiotics (such as ciprofloxacin, moxifloxacin, or ofloxacin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Levofloxacin can cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you use certain drugs (such as diuretics or water pills) or if you experience conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Levofloxacin may rarely cause significant changes in blood sugar levels, particularly if you have diabetes. Be vigilant for symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. Also, watch for symptoms of low blood sugar, such as sudden sweating, shaking, rapid heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling in the hands or feet. It is advisable to carry glucose tablets or gel to treat low blood sugar. If these are unavailable, quickly raise your blood sugar by consuming a fast source of sugar, such as sugar, honey, candy, fruit juice, or non-diet soda. Notify your doctor immediately about any reactions and the use of this medication. To prevent low blood sugar, eat meals on a regular schedule and avoid skipping meals. This drug may cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Do not drive, operate machinery, or perform tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication may increase your sensitivity to the sun. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Levofloxacin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (such as the typhoid vaccine). Children may be at greater risk for joint or tendon problems while using this drug. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Levofloxacin is very similar to ofloxacin. Avoid using medications containing ofloxacin while taking levofloxacin. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (such as urine screening for opiates), potentially causing false test results. Inform lab personnel and your doctors that you are using this drug. If someone has overdosed and has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Lab tests (such as kidney function, complete blood count, blood sugar, cultures) may be performed before and during treatment to monitor your progress or check for side effects. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Quinolone antibiotics, including levofloxacin, may cause serious and potentially permanent tendon damage (such as tendinitis or tendon rupture), nerve problems in the arms and legs (peripheral neuropathy), and nervous system problems. Tendon damage may occur during or after treatment with this medication. Stop exercising, rest, and seek medical help immediately if you develop joint, muscle, or tendon pain or swelling. This medication may worsen a certain muscle condition (myasthenia gravis). Levofloxacin is used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as quinolone antibiotics. This antibiotic treats only bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections (such as the common cold or flu). Read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist before you start taking levofloxacin and each time you get a refill. Take this medication by mouth on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after eating) as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. Take this medication at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after taking other products that may reduce its effectiveness. Examples include quinapril, sucralfate, vitamins/minerals (including iron and zinc), and products containing magnesium, aluminum, or calcium (such as antacids or calcium-enriched juice). Carefully measure the dose using a special measuring device/spoon. The dosage and length of treatment are based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For the best effect, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced times. Continue taking this medication until the full prescribed amount is finished, even if symptoms disappear after a few days. Nausea, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, lightheadedness, or trouble sleeping may occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has judged that the benefit to you is greater than the risk of side effects. This medication may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called C. difficile. This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. However, seek immediate medical attention if you notice symptoms of a serious allergic reaction, including rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. Always consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
